conclusion: In this local simulation without redaction the fake password was in 100% of simulated outgoing prompts and 100% of simulated log lines but only 55% of scripted answers under assumed copy rates (1/10 for summarize to 9/10 for debug-config), so a clean answer did not mean the password stayed out of the simulated transmission; redacting first gave 0% in prompts, 0% in logs and 0% in answers, and required facts were present in 100% of redacted versus 100% of unredacted scripted answers (a check that fell to 0% when README.md and notes.md were left out); how often a real model leaks is not measured here.
setup: local simulation only: scripted stand-in model, simulated sending and provider log, nothing transmitted; folder README.md + config.env + notes.md, canaries: password CANARY-7Q2X-FAKE (twice, incl. inside DATABASE_URL) and phone +1-555-0142 in free text, counted separately; 4 requests x 10 runs x 2 setups, seed 9009; assumed (not measured) copy chances summarize 0.1, debug-config 0.8, setup-guide 0.6, what-i-need 0.3, assumed quote-notes chances summarize 0.2, debug-config 0.1, setup-guide 0.4, what-i-need 0.3; redaction = 4 regex patterns with stable placeholders; usefulness = required facts from the true project present in the answer, with controls for changed facts and left-out files; exact string match
